title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #13

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a push? (1 mark)
   A. Pulling a cart
   B. Kicking a football
   C. Opening a drawer by its handle
   D. Drawing water with a rope

2. Which use of heat helps us on a cold morning? (1 mark)
   A. Growing shadows
   B. Making things dark
   C. Keeping us warm
   D. Making sound

3. Which of these is NOT an effect of force? (1 mark)
   A. Making something have colour
   B. Starting motion
   C. Changing shape
   D. Stopping motion

4. A pupil has hard dry faeces. Which is the best advice? (1 mark)
   A. Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
   B. Eat only white bread
   C. Stop drinking water
   D. Eat more sweets

5. Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction? (1 mark)
   A. Polishing a table
   B. Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor
   C. Oiling a floor
   D. Shoes with rough soles

6. Which of these helps farmers to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving canals leaking
   B. Drip irrigation
   C. Watering at noon
   D. Flooding the field

7. Which of these is a torch used for? (1 mark)
   A. To cool a room
   B. To make sound
   C. To give light in the dark
   D. To make food

8. Which of these sources of heat uses electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Charcoal jiko
   B. Firewood
   C. Electric iron
   D. The sun

9. Which of these do animals breathe in from the air? (1 mark)
   A. Smoke
   B. Oxygen
   C. Dust
   D. Water

10. Who should practise water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone at home and school
   B. Only farmers
   C. Only teachers
   D. Only adults

11. Why are cooking pots made of metal? (1 mark)
   A. Metal is soft
   B. Metal is light
   C. Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   D. Metal does not get hot

12. Which of these is true of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume
   B. It fills a room
   C. It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   D. It has no volume

13. Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food? (1 mark)
   A. Covering food
   B. Letting flies land on food
   C. Leaving food open
   D. Putting food on the floor

14. Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children? (1 mark)
   A. They grow more teeth
   B. They become taller
   C. They sleep too much
   D. They lose water quickly

15. Which of these is an example of reducing water wastage? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring leaks
   B. Leaving the hose on
   C. Closing a tap after use
   D. Washing with lots of water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same. (5 marks)

17. Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. (5 marks)

18. What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull. (2 marks)

19. Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Kicking a football
   A kick pushes the ball.

2. C — Keeping us warm
   Heat keeps our bodies warm.

3. A — Making something have colour
   Colour is not caused by a force.

4. A — Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
   Fibre and water help soften faeces.

5. D — Shoes with rough soles
   Rough soles grip the ground.

6. B — Drip irrigation
   Drip irrigation gives water directly to roots.

7. C — To give light in the dark
   A torch is an artificial light source.

8. C — Electric iron
   An electric iron uses electricity.

9. B — Oxygen
   Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

10. A — Everyone at home and school
   Everyone shares water and should save it.

11. C — Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   Metal passes heat from the fire to the food.

12. C — It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   A liquid has a fixed volume and takes the container's shape.

13. A — Covering food
   Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

14. D — They lose water quickly
   The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

15. C — Closing a tap after use
   Closing taps stops the flow of water.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.
